title: Explaining variation in sweat sodium concentration: effect of individual characteristics and exercise, environmental, and dietary factors
publisher: Journal of Applied Physiology (American Physiological Society)
claims: In 1,944 sweat tests from 1,304 subjects, whole-body sweat sodium concentration averaged 42.0 +/- 12.6 mmol/L (median 40.3), ranging from 17 to 106 mmol/L.
Whole-body sweating rate averaged 1.09 +/- 0.50 L/h, ranging from 0.19 to 5.64 L/h in this dataset.

Regression models explained only 17%-23% of the variation in whole-body sweat sodium; age group, race/ethnicity, fluid balance, sodium intake and relative VO2max had no association, so individual patch testing cannot easily be replaced by population averages.

Higher energy expenditure was associated with higher sweat sodium, and warmer months (used as a proxy for heat acclimatization) with lower sweat sodium; exercise mode, air temperature and sex may have small effects.
